answers.1_formula: Confirmed with one correction: margin is per leg, so the gross term is (m1 + m2) x cargo, not 2 x margin x cargo (equal only on symmetric pairs; Ashgate legs are 17 and 15). Per ship per cycle = ((m1+m2) x cargo - 2 x trip_cost - maintenance x 2 x travel / interval) / (2 x travel) = (m1+m2) x cargo / (2 x travel) - trip_cost / travel - maintenance / interval. Defaults: Tillam 280 - 110 - 50 = 120; Ashgate 320 - 160 = 160. Maintenance is smoothed by charging maintenance / maintenance_interval = 50 every cycle (no 3-cycle lump); closing a route just before the due cycle therefore saves nothing. Keep maintenance a multiple of the interval, or floor and carry the remainder.
answers.2_saturation: 5 credits off the sell price at the selling planet per extra ship, on both legs. Ship nets by order on one route: Tillam 120, 20, -80; Ashgate 160, 60, -40; permit-2 route 260, 160, 60, -40; permit-3 route 320, 220, 120, 20, -80. So the marginal ship reaches zero or below at the 3rd ship on a starter route, the 4th on permit 2, the 5th on permit 3. Whole-route net turns <= 0 (route idles) at the 4th ship on Tillam and the 5th on Ashgate, so a sloppy overload is a visible loss, not a freeze. Preview must show the marginal ship net before the player confirms.
answers.3_ship_and_start: ship_price 1000, starting_credits 1500. Second ship lands at cycle 5 on the first route (500 left + 160 per cycle), limit 6.
answers.4_rescue: rescue_stipend 1000 = ship_price. It cannot be farmed: there is no ship resale, so once a ship is owned the player can never be stranded (a free ship needs no cash to restart). Recommend the stranded test be 'owns zero ships and cash < ship_price', not 'no route earning': an event that closes Voltara blocks every starter route for event_interval cycles and must not pay a stipend. Even at zero ships it fires at most once per run.
answers.5_hoarding: No hoarding exploit. Idle ships cost nothing but also earn nothing, and every running ship nets above zero by the add-ship rule, so parking one only loses income. Maintenance is smoothed so timing closures does not help. Rule to add, not a number: a ship's first cycle on a route pays pro rata to the fraction of the cycle it was assigned, otherwise buying at the last second earns a full cycle (about 160 per ship). The sim assumes purchases at cycle start.
answers.6_pacing: See sim_results. Search method: throwaway paper model, whole-credit nets, settlement at every cycle end, buying at cycle start; best line = exhaustive search over permit timing with greedy best-marginal ship placement. Event Monte Carlo (400 seeds, pct 0.1 to 0.2, random planet, 4 cycles): best wins 89% (median 27, 1 win before 22), decent 81% (median 28), always_expand 1%, never_expand 0%.
answers.7_ashgate_permits: Ashgate left at energy_sell 27, food_buy 11 (+14% round-trip margin over Tillam, so two Voltara routes are a real choice). permit_margin_bonus 0.5 kept: +/-0.1 moves the best win by 1 to 2 cycles (0.4: 27 or 28, 0.6: 25), still in window. Permit routes are modelled as one new route each at +50% sell-side margin (see open question 1).
answers.8_events: event_effect = {pct:[0.1,0.2]}: one random planet, its sell prices x (1 +/- pct), rounded to whole credits, applied for event_interval cycles (until the next event, no new key). Example: Tillam -20% makes energy 24 -> 19, margin 9, first ship nets 70, second ship -30, so the route idles part of its ships. Closing a planet blocks its routes at zero cost, as the GDD says.
